newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish GPRD firm wants to enter bourse early 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish GPRD firm wants to enter bourse early 1997.

text.p: The Polish road construction firm Gdanskie Przedsiebiorstwo Robot Drogowych (GPRD) wants to enter the Warsaw Stock Exchange early next year, Nowa Europa daily quoted GPRD's financial director as saying.
"We would like to enter the bourse at the beginning of the next year. So far we don't know which market", Zygmunt Baranski said.

Nowa Europa said the company, based in Gdansk, northern Poland, wanted to offer new shares in a public subscription in October. Funds from the issue would be used to purchase modern equipment for motorways construction.
"We intend to participate in the motorways construction programme ... we have to buy more modern equipment and we need money for that," Nowa Europa quoted Baranski as saying.
The daily said GPRD had a net profit of 4.6 million zlotys and its turnover amounted to 82 million zlotys last year.
In 1996 the company was aiming to earn five million zlotys.
